Physical_Meaning: Density of pure, bubble-free solid glacier ice
Literature_Citation: Cuffey & Paterson (2010), The Physics of Glaciers, 4th ed., p. 12
Sensitivity_Justification: Standard glaciological uncertainty bounds for pure crystalline ice.
Provenance_Category: Category A: Published Physical Constant (Consensus)

Physical_Meaning: Reference density of polar ambient seawater at grounding lines
Literature_Citation: Jenkins (1991), J. Geophys. Res., 96(C11), 20671–20677; Jourdain et al. (2020), The Cryosphere, 14, 1147–1172
Sensitivity_Justification: Reflects polar shelf water salinity variations (34.2 to 34.8 PSU).
Provenance_Category: Category A: Published Physical Constant (Consensus)

Physical_Meaning: Acceleration due to gravity at 65-75 deg S
Literature_Citation: IUGG / WGS-84 Standard Gravitational Model at 70 deg S
Sensitivity_Justification: Variations across the Peninsula (< 0.1%) are negligible for ice dynamics.
Provenance_Category: Category A: Published Physical Constant (Consensus)

Physical_Meaning: Stress exponent for secondary dislocation creep in polycrystalline ice
Literature_Citation: Glen (1955), Proc. R. Soc. A, 228, 519–538; Cuffey & Paterson (2010), p. 60
Sensitivity_Justification: Standard sensitivity range in ice sheet flow models (Bueler & Brown 2009).
Provenance_Category: Category A: Published Physical Constant (Consensus)

Physical_Meaning: Arrhenius temperature-dependent rate factor for ice deformation
Literature_Citation: Cuffey & Paterson (2010), Table 3.4; Pattyn (2006), J. Geophys. Res., 111, F02004
Sensitivity_Justification: Supported directly by Cuffey & Paterson (2010) Table 3.4 for pure polycrystalline ice between -20 C and 0 C. Spatial ice temperature field across Peninsula basins is unconstrained and must be calibrated in Stage 1.
Provenance_Category: Category C: Theoretical Range & Category E: Stage 1 Calibration Target

Physical_Meaning: Power-law exponent relating basal shear traction to slip velocity
Literature_Citation: Weertman (1957), J. Glaciol., 3, 33–38; Schoof (2005, 2007); Gagliardini et al. (2007)
Sensitivity_Justification: Directly determines Schoof flux exponent gamma = (m+n+3)/(m+1).
Provenance_Category: Category C: Literature-Supported Theoretical Range

Physical_Meaning: Analytical power exponent relating grounding line flux to ice thickness
Literature_Citation: Schoof (2007), J. Fluid Mech., 573, Eq. 32; gamma = (m + n + 3) / (m + 1)
Sensitivity_Justification: Governs non-linear grounding line sensitivity to thickness perturbations.
Provenance_Category: Category C: Derived Analytic Property

Physical_Meaning: Basal slipperiness coefficient in Weertman traction law: tau_b = C_bed * u^m
Literature_Citation: Morlighem et al. (2020), Nature Geosci., 13, 132–137; Seroussi et al. (2014)
Sensitivity_Justification: InSAR ice-stream inversions exhibit broad spatial heterogeneity across several orders of magnitude. The range 1.0e7 to 5.0e10 is an analyst-selected calibration search interval for Stage 1 InSAR velocity matching.
Provenance_Category: Category C: Broad Literature Bounds & Category D/E: Analyst Search Interval for Stage 1 Calibration

Physical_Meaning: Geometric ice thickness at unperturbed grounding line position
Literature_Citation: BedMachine Antarctica V4.1 (Morlighem et al. 2020)
Sensitivity_Justification: Reflects BedMachine ice thickness measurement and interpolation uncertainty.
Provenance_Category: Category B: Observed Topographic Datum & Category D: Analyst Uncertainty Interval (+/- 50 m)

Physical_Meaning: Annual solid ice mass discharge across grounding line at steady state
Literature_Citation: Phase 3.2 Reconstruction; Gardner et al. (2018); Rignot et al. (2019)
Sensitivity_Justification: Reflects historical altimetry/InSAR consensus flux gate uncertainty.
Provenance_Category: Category B: Observed Consensus Reconstruction & Category D/E: Stage 1 Calibration Target

Physical_Meaning: Bedrock topography elevation relative to geoid at grounding line
Literature_Citation: BedMachine Antarctica V4.1 (Morlighem et al. 2020)
Sensitivity_Justification: Governs hydrostatic flotation condition H_flot = -(rho_w / rho_i) * z_b.
Provenance_Category: Category B: Observed Topographic Datum & Category D: Analyst Uncertainty Interval (+/- 50 m)

Physical_Meaning: Longitudinal slope of bedrock topography at grounding line: -dz_b/dx
Literature_Citation: BedMachine Antarctica V4.1; Schoof (2007)
Sensitivity_Justification: Determines Marine Ice Sheet Instability (MISI) onset when alpha_bed > 0.
Provenance_Category: Category B: Observed Topographic Gradient & Category D: Analyst Sensitivity Interval (+/- 25%)

Physical_Meaning: Dimensionless state variable scaling backstress: 1=full, 0=complete loss
Literature_Citation: Gudmundsson (2013), The Cryosphere, 7, 1133–1145; Fürst et al. (2016)
Sensitivity_Justification: Explores complete spectrum from unperturbed shelf to catastrophic collapse.
Provenance_Category: Category C: Dimensionless State Variable

Physical_Meaning: Proportion of longitudinal resistive stress supported by embayment margins
Literature_Citation: Fürst et al. (2016), Nature Climate Change, 6, 479–482; Reese et al. (2018)
Sensitivity_Justification: Fürst et al. (2016) and Reese et al. (2018) evaluate Antarctic-wide buttressing, but did not define this 1D scalar bounds. The interval [0.40, 0.85] was assumed by the analyst. InSAR surge calibrations in Larsen B (2.5-6x) require omega_b in [0.45, 0.70] for mu=1.5; omega_b=0.85 combined with mu=3.0 yields an uncalibrated theoretical surge of 296x.
Provenance_Category: Category D: Analyst-Selected Sensitivity Interval & Category E: Stage 1 Calibration Target

Physical_Meaning: Non-linear exponent in buttressed grounding-line flux equation
Literature_Citation: Gudmundsson (2013); Pegler (2018), J. Fluid Mech., 857, 605–647
Sensitivity_Justification: Gudmundsson (2013) and Pegler (2018) establish non-linear backstress matching, but do not specify a scalar exponent range [1.0, 3.0] for this bracketed equation. Range was assumed by the analyst to explore linear (1.0), intermediate (1.5-2.0), and cubic (3.0) response. Requires Stage 1 observational calibration.
Provenance_Category: Category D: Analyst-Selected Sensitivity Interval & Category E: Stage 1 Calibration Target

Physical_Meaning: Thermal driving for sub-shelf basal melting: T_cavity - T_freeze(z_draft)
Literature_Citation: Schmidtko et al. (2014), Science, 346, 1227–1231; Jourdain et al. (2020)
Sensitivity_Justification: Constrained strictly by observational hydrographic sections and reanalyses.
Provenance_Category: Category B: Observed Hydrographic Forcing & Category D: Analyst Scenario Interval

Physical_Meaning: Turbulent heat exchange velocity across sub-shelf boundary layer
Literature_Citation: Jenkins et al. (2010), J. Phys. Oceanogr., 40, 729–742; Jourdain et al. (2020)
Sensitivity_Justification: Supported directly by Jourdain et al. (2020) ISMIP6 thermal exchange benchmark (1.45e-4 m s^-1); broader interval 0.5e-4 to 2.0e-4 reflects boundary layer microphysical turbulence uncertainty.
Provenance_Category: Category C: Literature Baseline (ISMIP6 Benchmark)

Physical_Meaning: Isobaric specific heat capacity of polar ocean water
Literature_Citation: IOC, SCOR and IAPSO (2010), TEOS-10 Standard
Sensitivity_Justification: Thermodynamic property variation is negligible for cryospheric modeling.
Provenance_Category: Category A: Published Physical Constant (Consensus)

Physical_Meaning: Latent heat absorbed during ice melting at sub-shelf boundary
Literature_Citation: Cuffey & Paterson (2010), p. 12
Sensitivity_Justification: Thermodynamic universal constant.
Provenance_Category: Category A: Published Physical Constant (Consensus)

Physical_Meaning: RACMO2.3p2 net accumulation in water-equivalent (m w.e. yr^-1), converted to solid-ice accumulation rate a_dot_i = (rho_water / rho_i) * a_dot_we = 1.09051 * a_dot_we at rho_water=1000 kg m^-3, rho_i=917 kg m^-3
SI_Units: m w.e. yr^-1 (input); m ice-eq yr^-1 (solver); kg m^-2 s^-1 (mass flux)
Literature_Citation: RACMO2.3p2 (van Wessem et al. 2018); Phase 3.2 Reconstruction
Sensitivity_Justification: RACMO2.3p2 RCM net surface mass balance. Converted once upon staging using fresh water reference density rho_water=1000 kg m^-3. Sensitivity range +/- 15% is an analyst-selected interval reflecting regional snowfall/runoff uncertainty.
Provenance_Category: Category B: Observed Regional Climate Forcing & Category D: Analyst Sensitivity Interval (+/- 15%)

Physical_Meaning: Equivalent depth of pore space in firn layer above solid ice pore close-off
Literature_Citation: Ligtenberg et al. (2011), The Cryosphere, 5, 809–819; Kuipers Munneke et al. (2014)
Sensitivity_Justification: Controls firn buffering against meltwater ponding and hydrofracture.
Provenance_Category: Category B: Observed Regional Firn State & Category D: Analyst Sensitivity Interval

Physical_Meaning: Small velocity regularizer preventing singularity in Weertman basal drag beta_b and lateral drag beta_wall as u -> 0
Literature_Citation: Bueler & Brown (2009), J. Geophys. Res., 114, F03029; Jouvet (2023), J. Glaciol., 69, 102–114
Sensitivity_Justification: Ensures beta_b and beta_wall remain strictly finite at divide (u=0). At u_reg=1e-4 m yr^-1 (3.17e-12 m s^-1) with C_bed=1e7 Pa (m/s)^(-1/3), beta_b(0) = C_bed * u_reg^(-2/3) = 4.64e14 Pa s m^-1 (corrected from 4.64e10). At physical speeds (|u| >= 1 m yr^-1), relative perturbation is < 3.3e-9. Tested in Test 15.
Provenance_Category: Category C: Numerical Regularization Threshold
